# Integral Holonic Deep Synthesis: take a domain apart across its best exemplars, put it back together as one whole

> Button (= the result): **Wholeness** («Цельность»), the common denominator of the best solutions; input: a domain or a set of exemplars ([meta-template.md](./meta-template.md) §Console buttons, Sasha 2026-11-26). Earlier long form: *One whole, built from what works everywhere.* Repo file name: `docs/templates/integral-synthesis.md`. Routed by [template-router.md](./template-router.md). Template: meta-template. Draft v0, 2026-11-24, written by Evolver (Hark) in parallel with its first application, game navigation.
>
> Source: Sasha, 2026-11-24 (chat, verbatim): «Давай соберем интегральный глубинный синтез навигации в культовых играх... Возьмем их навигацию. Выделим инварианты задач которые они решают через общие знаменатели. Обратим внимание на самые успешные решения. Создадим интегральный холонический синтез из соответствия инварианту навигации и найденных успешных элементов которые вместе создают синергию цельности навигации не перегружая ее деталями. Можно сказать разбирают ее и собирают. Составляем параллельно ультра-подробный шаблон создания интегрального холонического глубинного синтеза, используя этот частный случай.»
>
> *Translation:* "Let's assemble an integral deep synthesis of navigation in iconic games. Take their navigation. Extract the invariants of the tasks they solve, through common denominators. Pay attention to the most successful solutions. Create an integral holonic synthesis from the fit to the invariant of navigation and the successful elements found, which together create a synergy of wholeness of navigation without overloading it with detail. You could say we take it apart and put it back together. In parallel we write an ultra-detailed template for creating an integral holonic deep synthesis, using this particular case."

## Meta-description
- **Level / parent:** L2 · Consciousness development (seeing instruments; same open question as [holonic-seeing.md](./holonic-seeing.md) whether seeing instruments sit directly under L0) · parent: [meta-template.md](./meta-template.md); engine for the seeing: [holonic-seeing.md](./holonic-seeing.md); engine for the critique: [roasting.md](./roasting.md); output compressed by: [holonic-prism.md](./holonic-prism.md)
- **Lens(es):** Ideal Forms (the invariant is the ideal form every exemplar approximates) with Causal (the phases, take apart then put together) and Unity (the synergy test: does the reassembled whole feel like one thing)
- **Shift carried (candidate, awaits Sasha):** PST 98 Prime Invariant Branding («Find the invariant. Everything else is a derivation.») · also PST 82 Linguistic Synthesis (simple, never simplistic), PST 164 Forecasting the Next Shift by the Invariant, PST 96 Signal-Preserving Holonic Artifact Propagation (one organizing principle) · **before:** a domain is designed by copying admired features one by one, or invented from scratch; the result is a pile of parts that each made sense somewhere else · **after:** the domain is seen as a small set of invariant tasks, each answered once by the best-proven solution, all derived from one organizing principle and nested level by level · **check:** (1) the owner says the whole in one sentence and, for any element, names the invariant it answers; (2) a first-time user passes the acceptance walk for the domain without a wall; (3) the element count went down or stayed while every core invariant is covered at every level
- **What emerges:** one synthesis document (the reassembled whole, its levels, its elements with evidence, its cut list, its deltas against today, and a short list of real decisions for the owner), plus a reusable invariant set for the domain
- **As a part of the whole:** the Meta-Template recognizing itself in other people's work: many exemplars are many projections of one ideal form; the synthesis finds the form and lets the target take it in its own material
- **Siblings / repeats:** [`../02-strategy/research/iconic-mechanics/template.md`](../02-strategy/research/iconic-mechanics/template.md) (Mechanic Transplant: one exemplar, many mechanics, bottom-up; this template is one domain, many exemplars, top-down by invariant; the evidence grades are shared and live there) and its [`synthesis.md`](../02-strategy/research/iconic-mechanics/synthesis.md) (precedent: survivors grouped into packages, each landing on one spec row); [source-integration.md](./source-integration.md) (how a single source is woven in; dossiers here may cite integrated sources); [name-vibration.md](./name-vibration.md) (the common-denominator move in miniature, across languages); [module-form.md](./module-form.md) and [spec-handoff.md](./spec-handoff.md) (downstream: where the synthesis lands and how it is built); [improvement-loop.md](./improvement-loop.md) (the retro)
- **Status · applied in · last reviewed:** draft v0 · first application: game navigation for The Game of Being You (in progress, project «Навигация по игре») · 2026-11-24

## Through the prism
- **Layer:** MODULE (a methodology). Serves: any PRODUCT whose part has to be designed well (navigation, onboarding, a session, a village). Carried by: the PROMPT layer (research agents with one dossier schema, Hark as keeper).
- **Essence:** many good answers to the same need are projections of one form; find the need, keep the best proven answer to each, rebuild them as one.
- **Significance:** it replaces both copying and inventing with recognition; the target gets the wisdom of the whole field without its clutter.
- **Consequences:** the owner decides a domain once, from a short list, with evidence; the user meets something that feels obvious, because every part answers a need they really have and nothing else is there.
- **One sentence:** Take a domain apart across its best exemplars, keep only the tasks every one of them must solve and the solutions proven to solve them, and put those back together around one principle so the whole works as one thing and carries nothing extra.
- **Passed down (to the agents):** every element you propose must name its invariant, its evidence grade and its level; anything that cannot is cut.

---

## 0. When to use, when not to use

**Use when**
- A domain (a function of a product) is solved by many well-known exemplars, and the target has to solve it too: navigation, onboarding, progression, social trust, a session format, a pricing page, a village layout.
- The current version of the domain in the target feels patched: parts added one by one, each defensible, the whole not.
- The owner asks to "take it apart and put it back together" («разобрать и собрать»).

**Do not use when**
- One exemplar has one mechanic worth moving: use [Mechanic Transplant](../02-strategy/research/iconic-mechanics/template.md).
- One source has to be integrated: use [source-integration.md](./source-integration.md).
- One artifact needs a next version: use [roasting.md](./roasting.md).
- There are fewer than about 6 exemplars with evidence: there is no common denominator to find; do a holonic seeing of the target instead.

**How it differs from Mechanic Transplant**
| | Mechanic Transplant | Integral Holonic Deep Synthesis |
|---|---|---|
| Unit of input | one game or product | one domain across many |
| Direction | bottom-up: mechanic → canon filter → spec row | top-down: invariant → best solution → whole → deltas |
| Output | candidate mechanics, each with priority | one reassembled whole, with what it replaces |
| Risk it guards against | adopting a mechanic without evidence | a pile of good parts that is not a whole |
Both share the A/B/C evidence grades (defined in the Mechanic Transplant template, rule 1; not repeated here).

---

## 1. Vocabulary (plain words)
| Word | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| **Domain** | the function being synthesized (navigation), not a screen |
| **Target whole** | the product the synthesis is for, with its canon and its current state |
| **Exemplar** | one iconic product (a game, or a series where the domain is the same) studied as a source |
| **Layer** | one part of an exemplar's domain the user can see and enter (world map, minimap, quest log) |
| **Task** | what a layer does for the user, written as the user's need ("know where I am") |
| **Common denominator** | what all the different forms of a task share once the form is removed; never the lowest common denominator (the weakest version everyone happens to ship) |
| **Invariant** | a task every serious exemplar must solve, in some form, at some level; it passes the tests in §7.4 |
| **Variant** | a task only some kinds of exemplar need; kept as "conditional on X" |
| **Solution** | one concrete way an exemplar answers a task (exact mechanics) |
| **Driver** | why a solution works, named as a known effect with a source |
| **Element** | a solution as it will exist in the target |
| **Organizing principle** | the one structure the elements are derived from |
| **Level (holon)** | a scale of the whole that is itself a whole: world, place, screen, moment |
| **Synergy** | elements that answer more together than apart: one element answering several invariants, or two elements reinforcing each other |
| **Overload** | an element, signal or detail that answers no invariant at that level, or answers one already answered |

---

## 2. Inputs, roles and the files it produces

**Inputs**
1. The domain, in the owner's words.
2. The target's canon (the documents that decide it) and its current state (what is built, what is broken).
3. The owner's constraints and standing rules (in GoBY: fidelity, real-life counterpart, no numbers that mirror nothing, the lock rule, approval rules for core flows).
4. A list of exemplars, or the owner's yes to the corpus Evolver proposes.

**Roles**
- **Owner (Sasha):** sets the domain and the order, decides the real forks (§14), says yes to any change of canon or core flows.
- **Keeper (Evolver / Hark):** frames, writes the schema, dispatches and checks the research, derives invariants, reassembles, roasts, writes the deliverable.
- **Research agents:** one per cluster of exemplars, all on the same schema, in parallel; they gather facts and grade them; they do not synthesize across clusters.

**Files (one folder per domain: `research/<domain>/`)**
| File | Holds | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `frame.md` | domain, target whole, canon, current state, acceptance walk, thresholds | §4 |
| `corpus.md` | exemplars, clusters, why each is in, negatives, out-of-domain controls | §5 |
| `SCHEMA.md` | the fixed dossier schema every agent fills | §6 |
| `exemplars/<cluster>.md` | the dossiers, one cluster per file, with cross-cluster patterns at the end | §6 |
| `invariants.md` | the invariant table, tree and order | §7 |
| `solutions.md` | the scored solution ledger | §8 |
| `matrix.md` | solutions × invariants | §9 |
| `synthesis.md` | **the deliverable**: principle, levels, elements, cut list, deltas, one sentence, decisions | §10–§16 |
| `sources.md` | every source with URL and access date (or sources stay inside dossiers; one place only) | all |

Single source of truth: a fact lives in its dossier; everything later links to it by exemplar and section, never copies it.

## 3. The phases at a glance
| # | Phase | Question it answers | Output | Gate (must be true before the next phase) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Frame | what are we synthesizing, for which whole, judged by what? | `frame.md` | the acceptance walk is written; canon and current state are linked |
| 2 | Corpus | which exemplars, why these? | `corpus.md` | variety rule met; negatives and controls included |
| 3 | Schema and decomposition | what does each exemplar do, layer by layer? | `SCHEMA.md`, `exemplars/*` | every dossier complete; every fact sourced; facts and *Judgment* separated |
| 4 | Invariants | which tasks must every exemplar solve? | `invariants.md` | each invariant passed the tests; 5–9 core |
| 5 | Evidence and success | which solutions are proven to work? | `solutions.md` | every candidate graded; no "best" on C alone |
| 6 | Matrix | which solutions answer which invariants? | `matrix.md` | every core invariant has at least one A or B solution, or is flagged |
| 7 | Organizing principle | what one structure do the elements derive from? | §1 of `synthesis.md` | every kept element derives from it |
| 8 | Holonic reassembly | how do the elements nest, level by level? | levels table + diagram | each invariant answered once per level; remove-one test passes |
| 9 | Subtraction | what is extra? | cut list | detail budget met per level |
| 10 | Fit to target | what changes in our product, and against which canon? | delta table | every delta mapped to canon and a spec row; conflicts listed, not resolved |
| 11 | Roast and crash-test | what is wrong with the whole? | roast notes, next version | meta-roast ends in one acceptance test |
| 12 | Prism and deliverable | what is it in one sentence? | `synthesis.md` complete | prism passes; length budget met |
| 13 | Decisions for the owner | what only the owner can decide? | decision list | only real forks; each with a recommendation |
| 14 | Retro and propagation | what did we learn about the method? | template update, PST candidates | template edited; candidates noted for Sasha |

No time estimates per phase (Sasha, 2026-11-21: we just do it). Phase 3 runs in parallel; everything else runs in order, but any phase can send the work back (§18 rule 7).

## 4. Phase 1 · Frame the domain and the target whole

**Purpose.** Fix what is being synthesized, for which whole, and how we will know the result works, before reading a single exemplar. A synthesis without a frame becomes a survey.

**Steps**
1. **Name the domain as a function**, in a verb: "how a player knows where they are, where they can go, what to do next, and how to get back", not "the menu".
2. **Name the target whole** and its level: which product, which part of it, what it serves above, what carries it below ([holonic-prism.md](./holonic-prism.md) step 1).
3. **Link the canon** that decides the domain today (sections, not documents). Mark each canon line as *binding* (owner-confirmed) or *draft*.
4. **Snapshot the current state**: what exists, by layer; what is broken; what is open. One file, dated, read from the source (code, live site), not from memory.
5. **Write the acceptance walk** for the domain: one concrete path a stranger must complete without a wall, with a start, an end and what "a wall" means. This is the test the whole will be judged by (it comes from [roasting.md](./roasting.md) §6: a meta-roast should end in one acceptance test; here we write a first version up front and let the roast sharpen it).
6. **Set thresholds** used later: what share of exemplars makes a task "ubiquitous" (default about 70%, across all clusters but one); the detail budget per level (default: one primary signal, at most two secondary, §12); the target count of core invariants (default 5–9).
7. **Name the owner's standing rules** that act as filters (approval rules, design laws).
8. **Name what is out of scope** (other domains that touch this one but are not it).

**Checklist**
- [ ] Domain written as a function, in the user's terms
- [ ] Target whole named with its level above and below
- [ ] Canon linked by section; binding vs draft marked
- [ ] Current state snapshot dated, read from the source
- [ ] Acceptance walk written (start, end, what counts as a wall)
- [ ] Thresholds set
- [ ] Standing rules and out-of-scope listed

**Gate.** Someone who has never seen the product can read `frame.md` and say what will be synthesized and how it will be judged.

**Anti-patterns.** Framing a screen instead of a function. Framing by the current build ("fix the rail") instead of by the need. Skipping the current state, so the synthesis cannot say what changes.

**Worked example: game navigation**
- Domain: how a player of The Game of Being You always knows where they are, where they can go and what opens it, what to do next and why, how to get there, what changed, what they have done, how to get back to safety, and how to see the whole. (Seed from SCHEMA Q1–Q9.)
- Target whole: GoBY navigation. Serves: the Journey and the village (the player becoming themselves in a real village). Carried by: title screen, village screen, rail, shell, module form.
- Canon (binding unless marked): GoBY §14.1 principles 1–5, 7, 10 ("The Journey is the spine"; "One world, one map, one menu. The village is the navigation"; "The village is where you play"; one module form; "Open is alive; closed is faded"; progress in the world, never in numbers; nothing internal on the surface); §13.1 village places; §14.2 Journey; §14.3 lock rule; §14.4 module form; §14.6. Draft: `player-path-v1-draft.md` (Player One as spine, Gift Path as progress scale), hypothesis only.
- Current state: [`nav_map_v0.md`](../02-strategy/research/navigation/nav_map_v0.md) (snapshot 2026-11-24): five layers (title, village with 11 places, rail = village places, shell with pane 2 on the old space ids, inside modules); known breaks (#443 A: rail greys out, Town Hall never navigates, pane 2 shows the wrong place, routes outside the shell, missing "← Village"); open questions to Sasha 2026-11-24: Q1 where-am-I = place or path step, Q2 the fate of pane 2, Q3 My AI = place or global button.
- Acceptance walk (draft, to sharpen in §13): *a stranger goes title → New Game → Entry Portal → village → their next move → one module → back to the village, sees what changed, and can say where they are and what is next, without a dead end, a wrong pane or a missing way back.*
- Thresholds: *fill.* Standing rules: core flows (title, intro, entry, reveal, themes) change only on Sasha's yes to the exact change; no numbers that mirror no real act. Out of scope: *fill* (for example the content inside each module).

## 5. Phase 2 · Choose the exemplar corpus

**Purpose.** Pick exemplars so that what they share is a property of the domain, not of one genre, one era or one studio.

**Selection criteria (each exemplar must meet 1 and 2, and the corpus as a whole must meet 3–7)**
1. **Iconic:** lasting reputation (sales, longevity, critical consensus, influence on later designs). Note which.
2. **Known for this domain:** its solution in the domain was praised, copied or notoriously criticized. An iconic product with an unremarkable domain teaches little.
3. **Variety (maximum variation):** clusters that differ in structure (for navigation: open world, hub-and-spoke, metroidvania, strategy meta-map, town or life sim, MMO or social, mobile and location-based, narrative). Variety is what makes a shared task an invariant.
4. **Negative exemplars:** at least 2 products whose domain famously failed. Failures show which tasks are necessary (the absence test, §7.4 T3).
5. **Out-of-domain controls:** 1–3 sources outside the product category that face the same need (for navigation: real-world wayfinding, city legibility, airport signage, map design). They test whether a task is a property of people, not of games.
6. **Closest to target:** at least 2 exemplars structurally close to the target (for GoBY: a village or town as the main screen, places that open over time).
7. **Evidence available:** enough public material (data, talks, interviews, reviews) to grade claims. A legendary product with no evidence enters as C only.

**Size and saturation.** Start with 12–30 exemplars in 4–8 clusters. Stop adding when the last 3–4 dossiers bring no new task (saturation). If a new cluster brings a new task, it is not saturated.

**Corpus table (in `corpus.md`)**
| # | Exemplar (years, studio, lead designer) | Cluster | Criteria met (1–7) | Why it is in, one line | Role: core / negative / control / closest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Checklist**
- [ ] Every exemplar meets criteria 1 and 2
- [ ] At least 4 structurally different clusters
- [ ] At least 2 negatives, 1 control, 2 closest-to-target
- [ ] Series grouped only where the domain is the same; split where it changed
- [ ] The owner's own list (if any) included as given; additions marked as Evolver's

**Gate.** No single cluster holds more than about a third of the corpus.

**Anti-patterns.** Genre monoculture (all open-world games: every invariant comes out as "a big map"). Survivorship only (no failures). Favourites over evidence. Including the target's direct competitors only.

**Worked example: game navigation**
*Fill from the research run: the corpus table, clusters and roles.* Cluster kinds to cover (illustrative, replace with the actual run): open world; hub-and-spoke; metroidvania; strategy meta-map; town or life sim; MMO or social; mobile and location-based; narrative. Controls: *fill* (real-world wayfinding sources). Closest to target: *fill* (village or town as main screen). Negatives: *fill*.

## 6. Phase 3 · Fixed schema, then decompose every exemplar

**Purpose.** Take each exemplar apart the same way, so the parts can be laid side by side. Comparability is the whole point: a free-form dossier cannot be cross-read.

### 6.1 The schema (write once, before dispatch; every agent fills the same one)
A dossier schema has six parts. Adapt the content to the domain, keep the shape.
1. **Header:** exemplar, years, studio, lead designer; which titles it covers and why grouped.
2. **Layers, outermost to innermost:** a table *layer | what the user sees | what task it solves | how you enter and leave it*. Outermost to innermost makes the nesting visible, which §11 needs.
3. **Answers to the seed task questions:** one line each, or "not addressed". The seed list is the keeper's first hypothesis of the invariants, written from the frame. It **must end with an open question** ("anything else this exemplar solves that the list misses: add a new question"), so the schema can find tasks the keeper did not think of. "Not addressed" is data, not a gap.
4. **The 1–3 most successful solutions:** exact mechanics; evidence it worked with grade A/B/C (definitions: [Mechanic Transplant, rule 1](../02-strategy/research/iconic-mechanics/template.md)); the driver (why it works, a named effect); source URL and date.
5. **Known failures and criticism**, with sources.
6. **Designer intent quotes**, verbatim, with source.
At the end of each cluster file: **cross-exemplar patterns in this cluster** (5–10 bullets: candidate invariants and recurring best solutions). This is the first, local common denominator.

**Rules for agents (put them in every dispatch).** Same schema, no extra sections. Cite every fact with a URL. Mark *Judgment* separately from facts. Dense, no filler; a word budget per major exemplar (default 600–1,200). Web search and fetch only unless a source needs a browser. Do not synthesize across clusters; that is the keeper's job.

### 6.2 Dispatch
One agent per cluster, in parallel, each with: the schema file, its cluster's exemplars, the frame (so they know the target), the word budget, and where to write. The keeper does not start §7 (invariants) on partial clusters, except to note early patterns.

### 6.3 Check each dossier on arrival
- [ ] All six parts present for every exemplar; layer table outermost to innermost
- [ ] Every seed question answered or marked "not addressed"
- [ ] Open question used (new tasks listed, or "none found")
- [ ] Each "successful solution" has mechanics + grade + driver + source
- [ ] At least one failure or criticism per exemplar (if none was found, say so)
- [ ] Facts and *Judgment* separated; no uncited numbers
- [ ] Cluster patterns written
A dossier that fails the check goes back to its agent with the failing items, not fixed silently by the keeper.

**Gate.** All clusters pass the check.

**Anti-patterns.** Schema drift (agents adding their own sections). Praise without evidence ("beloved map"). Describing the screen instead of the task. Copying marketing copy as fact.

**Worked example: game navigation**
The schema is [`SCHEMA.md`](../02-strategy/research/navigation/SCHEMA.md) (project workspace `research/nav/SCHEMA.md`; proposed repo home next to the other research). It shows the six parts: layers (front-end menu, world map, hub, playfield, HUD, journal, inventory, fast travel, save/return home); seed questions Q1 Where am I? Q2 Where can I go, and what opens it? Q3 What should I do next, and why? Q4 How do I get there? Q5 What changed since I was last here? Q6 What have I done, where have I been? Q7 How do I return to safety, home, save? Q8 How do I see the whole, zoom between scales? Q9 How do I switch modes without getting lost? and the open Q10; top 1–3 solutions graded A/B/C with driver; failures; designer quotes; cross-game patterns per cluster.
Dossiers: *fill: list of `exemplars/<cluster>.md` files and their check status.*

## 7. Phase 4 · Derive the task invariants by common denominator

**Purpose.** Find the few tasks every serious exemplar must solve, stripped of the forms they take. This is the "ideal form" the target will answer.

### 7.1 Collect
Pull every task from every dossier: the "task it solves" column of each layer table, every seed answer, every new question from the open slot, every cluster pattern. One row per (exemplar, task, form).

### 7.2 Normalize
Rewrite each task as the user's need, verb first, no form words: "know where I am", not "minimap". Keep the form in its own column. Two tasks with the same need and different forms become one row with two forms.

### 7.3 Group by common denominator
For each group, ask: **what is left when the form is removed?** That remainder is the common denominator. Write it in one line. If the remainder is empty or vague ("good UX"), the group is not a task: split it or drop it.
Guard: **common denominator, never lowest common denominator.** The denominator is the shared need, not the weakest shared form. "Every game has a pause menu" is a shared form; "the user can always get back to safety" is the shared need.

### 7.4 Test each candidate (all seven; record each result)
| # | Test | Question | Passes when |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | **Ubiquity** | is it addressed across the corpus? | addressed in at least the threshold share of exemplars (default ~70%), in all clusters but at most one |
| T2 | **Form independence** | is it solved in different ways? | at least 2–3 distinct forms; a task with one form everywhere may be a convention, not a need |
| T3 | **Absence (necessity)** | when an exemplar did not solve it, did it hurt? | criticism, failure or player workarounds appear where it is missing (negatives help here) |
| T4 | **Out of domain** | do people face it outside this product category? | a control source (for navigation: real-world wayfinding) names the same need |
| T5 | **Irreducibility** | can it be derived from another invariant? | no; if yes, it becomes a child of that invariant |
| T6 | **Scale** | does it hold at more than one level (world, place, screen)? | yes = a holonic invariant (answered at each level); no = a level-specific invariant (answered once, at its level) |
| T7 | **Target relevance** | does the target's user face it? | yes, in the target's own terms; a true invariant of the field the target does not face is recorded and parked |
Verdict per candidate: **core** (passes T1–T5 and T7), **conditional** (fails T1 only because one cluster does not need it: write "conditional on X" and check whether the target is an X), **child** (fails T5: nest it), **rejected** (fails T2 or T3: a convention or a fashion; record why).

### 7.5 Shape the set
- **Count:** aim for 5–9 core invariants. More than 9: look for parents (T5) and merge. Fewer than 5: the grouping was too coarse, or the domain is narrow; check the open-question tasks again.
- **Tree:** parents and children (for example "see the whole" may parent "zoom between scales").
- **Order:** which invariant depends on which (the user cannot choose where to go before knowing where they are). The order becomes the reading order of the synthesis and often the order of the acceptance walk.
- **Name each invariant twice:** the need in plain words, and the question the user asks ("Where am I?").

### 7.6 Output (`invariants.md`)
| ID | Invariant (the need) | The user's question | Common denominator (what all forms share) | Forms seen (exemplar refs) | Presence n/N, clusters | T1–T7 results | Scale(s) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
Then: the tree, the order, the rejected list with reasons, and the tasks parked under T7.

**Checklist**
- [ ] Every task from every dossier landed in a group or the rejected list
- [ ] Every common denominator is one line and form-free
- [ ] All seven tests recorded per candidate
- [ ] 5–9 core; tree and order drawn
- [ ] At least one invariant came from the open question (or a line saying none did, and why that is plausible)

**Gate.** Read only the invariant names to someone outside the project: they recognize each as a real need they have had.

**Anti-patterns.** Form as invariant ("a minimap"). Seed list taken as the answer (confirmation bias; the open question exists to break it). Counting only ubiquity (a fashion is ubiquitous too: T3 catches it). Too many invariants (a checklist, not a form).

**Worked example: game navigation**
Seed hypotheses: Q1–Q9 from the schema. *Fill: the invariant table after the dossiers arrive; the tree; the order; the rejected list; what the controls (real-world wayfinding) confirmed or added.* Expected early tension to test, not assume: whether "what changed" (Q5) and "what have I done" (Q6) are one invariant (the trace) or two.

## 8. Phase 5 · Evidence grading and success selection

**Purpose.** For each invariant, find the solutions that are proven to work, and separate "this solution worked" from "this game was a hit".

### 8.1 Grade every claim
Use A / B / C exactly as defined in [Mechanic Transplant, rule 1](../02-strategy/research/iconic-mechanics/template.md) (A: controlled study or large-n data; B: hard observational numbers, telemetry, a talk with data; C: designer interview, critical consensus, fan memory). Grade the claim about the solution, not the exemplar's fame.

### 8.2 Score each candidate solution (`solutions.md`)
| Factor | Scale | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| **Evidence** | A = 3, B = 2, C = 1 | the strongest graded claim that this solution did its job |
| **Convergence** | 0–2 | 0: one exemplar; 1: copied by 2–3 others; 2: became an industry convention after it appeared (diffusion is evidence that it worked for many teams) |
| **Driver** | 0–2 | 0: no reason known; 1: a plausible named effect; 2: a named effect with its own research |
| **Attribution** | 0–2 | how much of the observed success this solution plausibly explains (separate it from the exemplar's other strengths, as Mechanic Transplant rule 3 does) |
| **Failure record** | 0 to −2 | documented harm, misuse, criticism, or a later reversal by the same studio |
Score = sum. A solution is a **best candidate** for an invariant when it is in the top 1–3 for that invariant **and** its evidence is A or B. A C-only solution can be kept as a candidate, never as the only answer to a core invariant.

### 8.3 Rules
- **Evidence about the solution, not the product.** A best-selling game with a criticized map does not lend its sales to its map.
- **Negative evidence counts.** A solution that failed somewhere enters the ledger with its failure, so §11 can avoid it.
- **One ledger line per solution form**, with every exemplar that uses it, so convergence is countable.
- **No invented numbers.** A missing number is written as missing.

**Checklist**
- [ ] Every "most successful solution" from the dossiers is in the ledger
- [ ] Every ledger line has a grade, a driver (or "unknown") and a source
- [ ] Each core invariant has at least one candidate; flag the ones with no A or B
- [ ] Failures recorded next to the solutions they belong to

**Gate.** No core invariant rests on C alone without a flag in the deliverable.

**Anti-patterns.** Halo (a great game's every feature called great). Recency (the newest solution assumed better). Counting fan love as evidence of function.

**Worked example: game navigation**
*Fill: the solution ledger.* Ledger columns to keep: solution form · exemplars using it · invariant(s) it answers · grade · convergence · driver · attribution · failures · score · source refs (dossier § only; facts stay in dossiers).

---

## 9. Phase 6 · Map solutions × invariants

**Purpose.** See at a glance which solutions answer which needs, where they overlap and where they fight. The matrix is where synergy and overload first become visible.

### 9.1 Build it (`matrix.md`)
Rows: candidate solutions (from §8, with score). Columns: core invariants (in their order), then conditional ones. Cells: **●** primary answer, **○** partial or supporting, blank = none. Add a column *level(s)* (world / place / screen / moment) and a column *conflicts with*.

### 9.2 Read it (write each reading under the matrix)
1. **Multi-answer solutions:** rows with ● or ○ in several invariants. These are synergy candidates: one element, several needs.
2. **Gaps:** invariants with no ● from an A or B solution. These are risks, or places the target may have to invent (and then test).
3. **Redundancy:** invariants with many ● rows. Only one will survive per level (§10); the rest are overload candidates.
4. **Conflicts:** pairs of solutions that pull against each other (for navigation: full freedom to wander vs a strong arrow to the next goal). Name the trade-off; the organizing principle (§10) or the owner decides it.
5. **Level spread:** which levels each invariant is answered at across the corpus (this feeds §10).

**Gate.** Every reading written; every gap and conflict listed by name.

**Anti-patterns.** A matrix with no readings (decoration). Treating ● counts as votes.

**Worked example: game navigation**
*Fill: the matrix and its five readings.*

---

## 10. Phase 7 · Find the one organizing principle

**Purpose.** Find the single structure the kept elements derive from, so the whole is one thing and not a set (PST 98: "Find the invariant. Everything else is a derivation."; PST 96: every artifact has an organizing principle).

**Steps**
1. From the matrix, list the 2–4 structures that answer the most invariants at once (often a multi-answer solution generalized: "the world is the menu", "the path is the map").
2. Check the target's canon for a principle that already exists. If one exists, test it first; the synthesis may confirm, sharpen or challenge it.
3. **Derivation test:** for each candidate principle, try to derive every best-candidate element from it ("given this principle, the answer to *where am I* is…"). Count what derives, what does not, and what it makes unnecessary.
4. **Conflict test:** does the principle settle the conflicts from §9.2 (4)? A good principle dissolves trade-offs instead of picking sides.
5. **Out-of-domain test:** does the principle make sense in the control sources (does real-world wayfinding work this way)?
6. Choose one. Write it as one sentence a stranger understands, plus one line on what it rules out.
7. If two principles survive equally, that is a real fork: it goes to the owner (§16) with both derivations.

**Output.** §1 of `synthesis.md`: *Organizing principle* (one sentence) · *what it rules out* · *derivation table* (element → how it follows) · *what did not derive and why* (each such element is either cut in §12 or a sign the principle is incomplete).

**Gate.** Every element that will be kept is derived from the principle, or explicitly marked as an exception with a reason.

**Anti-patterns.** A slogan as principle (it derives nothing). Two principles held at once without saying so. Overriding a binding canon principle silently.

**Worked example: game navigation**
Existing canon candidate to test first: GoBY §14.1.2 "One world, one map, one menu. The village is the navigation." together with §14.1.1 "The Journey is the spine." Note the open fork already sent to Sasha on 2026-11-24 (Q1: where-am-I as place or as path step): the principle the synthesis finds will bear on it. *Fill: candidates from the matrix, derivation and conflict tests, the chosen principle.*

---

## 11. Phase 8 · Holonic reassembly, level by level

**Purpose.** Put the elements back together so each level is a whole in itself and a part of the level above, with the same principle showing at every scale.

### 11.1 Define the levels
List the levels of the target from outermost to innermost (for a product: world → place → screen → moment), taken from the target's own structure and checked against the exemplars' layer tables. Usually 3–5 levels. Each level gets one line: what a whole is at this level.

### 11.2 Fill the levels table
| Level | What is a whole here | Invariants answered here | Element that answers each (one per invariant) | Evidence (solution ID, grade) | Enter from / leave to | Inherits from above | Passes down |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### 11.3 Reassembly rules
1. **One answer per invariant per level.** Each invariant that applies at a level is answered there by exactly one primary element. Other elements may support it (○) but never compete with it. This is the single-source-of-truth rule applied to the user's attention.
2. **Same grammar at every scale.** A holonic invariant (T6) is answered by the same kind of element at each level (for example the same open/faded rule for a place, a room and a button). The user learns it once.
3. **Transitions are elements.** Going in and out of a level (zoom in, back, return home) is designed and evidenced like any other element; a level with no way out is a wall.
4. **Prefer multi-answer elements** (from §9.2 (1)) when they are A/B evidenced: fewer elements, more synergy.
5. **Every element names its invariant, its evidence and its level.** An element that cannot is not in.
6. **Derive, do not decorate.** Every element follows from the organizing principle (§10).
7. **Keep what the target already does well**, if it answers an invariant with evidence at least as good as the best candidate; change only where the synthesis is stronger.

### 11.4 Synergy tests (record results)
- **Remove-one test (necessity):** remove each element in turn; if no invariant loses its answer at any level, the element is extra (send to §12).
- **Add-nothing test (sufficiency):** every core invariant is answered at every level it applies to.
- **Reinforcement test:** list pairs of elements that make each other stronger (the same landmark seen on the map and in the place; the next move shown where the user already looks). A whole with no reinforcing pairs is a set, not a synergy.
- **Emergence test:** name, in one line, what the whole does that no element does alone. If nothing, the reassembly is a list.

### 11.5 Output
The levels table, a diagram (nested boxes or a short tree, text is fine), the synergy test results, and the emergent property line. This is §2 of `synthesis.md`.

**Checklist**
- [ ] Levels named, 3–5, outermost to innermost
- [ ] Each applicable invariant answered once per level
- [ ] Transitions designed for every level
- [ ] Remove-one, add-nothing, reinforcement, emergence tests recorded

**Gate.** A reader can start at any level and answer every user question for that level from the table alone.

**Anti-patterns.** Frankenstein (the best piece from each exemplar bolted together, each with its own grammar). Average of everything (every solution half-kept). Levels that do not nest (a screen that belongs to no place).

**Worked example: game navigation**
Levels to test (from the target's own structure, `nav_map_v0.md`): world (title screen as the only door; the village as the world) → place (one of 11 village places) → room or module (Intro → one button → result → Outro) → moment (the one button, the next-move card). Whether the Journey path is its own level or a view over the world is the Q1 fork. *Fill: levels table, diagram, synergy results, emergent property line.*

---

## 12. Phase 9 · Subtraction pass (no overload)

**Purpose.** Remove everything that does not carry weight, so the whole stays simple without becoming simplistic (PST 82: every remaining element is load-bearing; removing any one loses meaning).

**Steps**
1. **Run remove-one again** on the reassembled whole; cut every element that fails it.
2. **Detail budget per level:** at any one moment, one primary navigation signal and at most two secondary ones (default set in §4; adjust for the domain). Count what the user sees on each level's main screen; cut or defer the excess.
3. **Redundancy sweep:** for each invariant, list every element that touches it; keep the primary, keep supports only if they reinforce (§11.4), cut the rest.
4. **"Would they miss it?"** For each remaining secondary element: would a first-time user, on the acceptance walk, notice its absence? If not, defer it.
5. **Simple vs simplistic check:** for each cut, confirm no invariant lost its answer and no level lost its exit. If one did, the cut was simplistic: restore the minimum that answers it.
6. **Write the cut list**, each line with its reason and its fate: *cut* (never), *deferred* (later version, named), *kept as option for the owner* (only if the owner's taste may differ).

**Output.** §3 of `synthesis.md`: the cut list (element · reason · fate) and the detail count per level before and after.

**Gate.** Every level is within budget; no invariant or exit was lost.

**Anti-patterns.** Cutting the transitions (they look small and are load-bearing). Cutting the only answer to a gap invariant because its evidence is C (flag it instead). Keeping something because an iconic exemplar has it.

**Worked example: game navigation**
*Fill: the cut list and the before/after count per level.* Candidates to check against the current state: pane 2 on the old space ids (Q2 fork), duplicated places between rail and map (canon already says they are one), My AI as place and as global button (Q3 fork).

---

## 13. Phase 10 · Fit to the target canon and current state

**Purpose.** Turn the reassembled whole into concrete changes to the real product, without breaking its canon or deciding what only the owner decides.

**Steps**
1. **Canon filter** each kept element: run the target's own filter (for GoBY: the canon filter in [Mechanic Transplant §3](../02-strategy/research/iconic-mechanics/template.md): §10a fidelity, §21.2 real-life counterpart, §15.8 new facet, the almanac design rule, "already in canon?", and the standing rule that a number appears only where it mirrors a real act). Verdict per element: pass / pass with change (say which) / reject (say why, keep the row).
2. **Delta table** against the current state:
| Element | Level | Invariant | Today (current state ref) | Synthesis | Delta: keep / change / add / remove | Canon § it rests on | Spec row or issue it lands on | Needs owner's yes? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
3. **Mark every delta that touches a protected flow** (for GoBY: title screen, intro, entry, reveal, themes, how a player enters the game): it needs the owner's yes to the exact change; it goes to §16, never into a build.
4. **Mark every conflict with binding canon:** the synthesis may show canon is wrong; that is a decision for the owner, stated with evidence, never resolved silently.
5. **Group deltas into packages** that each land on one place in the spec (precedent: the four packages in [iconic-mechanics/synthesis.md](../02-strategy/research/iconic-mechanics/synthesis.md)), so they can be decided and built one at a time.
6. **Plain bugs** found on the way (a broken route) are listed separately; they may already be in the keeper's zone to fix under standing grants, and they are not the synthesis.

**Gate.** Every delta has a canon reference, a landing place and an approval flag.

**Anti-patterns.** Writing specs before the owner decides the forks. Hiding a canon change inside a "polish" delta. Mixing bug fixes with redesign.

**Worked example: game navigation**
*Fill: canon filter results, delta table against `nav_map_v0.md`, packages.* Known protected flows here: title screen and intro, entry portal, how a player enters the game. Known bugs to keep separate: #443 A items.

---

## 14. Phase 11 · Roast and crash-test the whole

**Purpose.** See everything wrong with the reassembled whole before anyone builds it.

**Steps (run [roasting.md](./roasting.md), do not restate it)**
1. **Holonic seeing first** ([holonic-seeing.md](./holonic-seeing.md) Round 1): the whole from the 12 positions; watch the AI bias toward UR (does it work?) and LR (does it scale?); lead the correction with UL (does it feel true to the user?) and LL (would the tribe recognize itself?).
2. **Roast 1, roast 2, meta-roast**, no fixing (roasting.md §3).
3. **Crash-test with personas** (roasting.md §4 posture: busy, distracted, skeptical humans): a first-time user; a user returning after two weeks; a user on a phone; a power user; for GoBY also a player arriving from a shared link into the middle of the world. For each: where do they get lost, and why did it die?
4. **Meta-roast ends in one acceptance test** (roasting.md §6): sharpen the acceptance walk from §4 into the test every future build of this domain must pass.
5. **Synthesis:** the next version of `synthesis.md`, carrying what the roast saw. Repeat up to 3 cycles; stop at kinetic calm.

**Gate.** The acceptance test is written in its final form; every persona has a path with no wall, or the wall is a named decision.

**Worked example: game navigation**
*Fill: roast notes (or a link), persona results, the final acceptance test.*

---

## 15. Phase 12 · The prism and the deliverable

**Purpose.** Compress the whole into one sentence and one short document the owner can decide from.

**Steps**
1. Run [holonic-prism.md](./holonic-prism.md) on the synthesis. If the one sentence does not fit, the synthesis is not done: go back to §10.
2. Write `synthesis.md` in this shape (length budget: the body fits in about two screens; everything else is linked):

```markdown
# <Domain> for <target>: integral holonic synthesis

Date · Status: draft | reviewed by <owner> | adopted · Template: integral-synthesis
Corpus: N exemplars in K clusters (link corpus.md) · Invariants: n core (link invariants.md)

## The whole in one sentence
<prism one sentence>

## 1. Organizing principle
<one sentence> · Rules out: <one line> · Derivation: <short table or link>

## 2. The whole, level by level
<levels table> · <diagram> · Emergent property: <one line>

## 3. What we cut and why
<cut list, short> · Detail count per level: before → after

## 4. What changes in our product
<delta table grouped by package; approval flags>

## 5. Acceptance test
<the walk, final form>

## 6. Decisions for <owner>
<decision list, §16>

## 7. Evidence and gaps
Core invariants resting on C only: <list> · Gaps the target must invent and test: <list>

Sources: dossiers (exemplars/*), solutions.md, matrix.md.
```

**Gate.** Prism passes; every claim in the body links to a dossier, the ledger or the matrix; facts and *Judgment* still separated.

**Anti-patterns.** A survey of exemplars as the deliverable (the dossiers are the appendix, not the result). A long report the owner cannot decide from (Sasha, 2026-11-22: a brief only for a real decision).

---

## 16. Phase 13 · Decision list for the owner

**Purpose.** Bring the owner only what only the owner can decide, each with a recommendation, so a few words answer it.

**What goes here.** Ties between organizing principles; deltas touching protected flows; conflicts with binding canon; gaps with no A/B evidence where the target must invent; anything the owner's standing rules reserve. **What does not:** anything the frame, canon and evidence already settle (settle it, report it).

**Format (one line per decision)**
| # | Decision | Options | My recommendation | Why (evidence ref) | Confidence | What it unblocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Gate.** Every item is a real fork; none is answerable from earlier decisions; each has a recommendation.

**Worked example: game navigation**
Already open with Sasha (2026-11-24): Q1 where-am-I = place or path step; Q2 the fate of pane 2; Q3 My AI as place or global button. The synthesis should answer them with evidence or sharpen them. *Fill: the final decision list.*

---

## 17. Phase 14 · Retro and propagation
1. **Update this template** with what the run taught (meta-template §7.4): which test caught what, where the schema was weak, what the thresholds should be.
2. **Note whether the shift check was seen** (Meta-description): could the owner say the whole in one sentence and name each element's invariant? did the acceptance walk pass?
3. **PST candidates:** any new law found (for example a navigation invariant that turns out to hold for every domain) is noted here and brought to Sasha (meta-template §7.8).
4. **Reuse:** the invariant set of this domain is kept as a starting seed for the next synthesis of the same domain; the schema becomes the domain's standard schema.

---

## 18. Cross-cutting rules
1. **Facts, *Judgment*, decisions never mixed.** Every fact has a source and date; every reading is marked *Judgment*; every choice the owner makes is dated with their words.
2. **Single source of truth.** Facts live in dossiers; later files link to them.
3. **Evidence before taste.** No element enters without a graded claim or an explicit "invented here, to test".
4. **The owner's rules are filters, not suggestions.** Approval rules and canon apply in every phase.
5. **Nothing touches the repo** (commits, issues, credits) until the owner says yes to the exact change; plain bugs follow the standing grants.
6. **Plain words, no em dashes**, English in artifacts; the owner's quotes stay verbatim in their language with a translation.
7. **Send back, do not paper over.** Any phase can return the work to an earlier one: a missing invariant found in the roast goes back to §7; an underived element goes back to §10.

## 19. Master quality checklist
- [ ] Frame: function-named domain, target whole, canon by section, current state dated, acceptance walk, thresholds
- [ ] Corpus: variety, negatives, controls, closest-to-target; saturation reached
- [ ] Decomposition: one schema, every dossier passed the check, open question used
- [ ] Invariants: common denominators form-free, seven tests recorded, 5–9 core, tree and order
- [ ] Evidence: every solution graded; no core invariant on C alone without a flag
- [ ] Matrix: five readings written
- [ ] Principle: one sentence; everything kept derives from it
- [ ] Reassembly: one answer per invariant per level; transitions designed; synergy tests passed; emergent property named
- [ ] Subtraction: within budget; cut list with reasons; nothing simplistic
- [ ] Fit: canon filter, delta table, packages, protected flows flagged
- [ ] Roast: holonic seeing, roasts, personas, final acceptance test
- [ ] Deliverable: prism one sentence, two-screen body, links not copies
- [ ] Decisions: only real forks, each with a recommendation
- [ ] Retro: template updated, shift check noted, PST candidates noted

## 20. Anti-patterns (the whole list)
| Anti-pattern | What it looks like | Caught by |
|---|---|---|
| Feature soup | the best feature of every exemplar, all kept | §11 rule 1, §12 |
| Frankenstein | parts with different grammars bolted together | §10 derivation test, §11 rule 2 |
| Average of everything | every solution half-kept | §11 rule 1 |
| Lowest common denominator | the weakest shared form taken as the answer | §7.3 guard |
| Form as invariant | "a minimap" instead of "know where I am" | §7.2, T2 |
| Fashion as invariant | ubiquitous, but nothing breaks without it | T3 |
| Genre monoculture | invariants of one genre called universal | §5 criterion 3 |
| Survivorship | only hits studied | §5 criterion 4 |
| Halo | a great game's every part called great | §8.3 |
| Seed confirmation | the seed questions come back as the invariants, nothing new | §6.1 open question, §7 checklist |
| Simplistic | cut until an invariant or an exit is lost | §12 step 5 |
| Canon-blind | a whole that ignores the target's binding rules | §13 |
| Silent canon change | a redesign hidden in a polish delta | §13 steps 3–4 |
| Survey as result | the deliverable describes exemplars | §15 |
| Decision flood | the owner gets every fork | §16 |
| AI bias | the whole works mechanically, feels like nothing | §14 step 1 |
